gloss: my home; my place; my family

definitions.gloss: my home; my place; my house; my family
definitions.explanation: A colloquial word for one's own home or household. Refers to the speaker's residence or family group, and is the everyday spoken counterpart to {家|いえ}.

examples.japanese: うちは{駅|えき}から{近|ちか}い。
examples.english: My place is close to the station.

examples.japanese: {今度|こんど}うちに{遊|あそ}びに{来|き}て。
examples.english: Come over to my place next time.

examples.japanese: うちの{父|ちち}はサラリーマンで、{母|はは}は{看護師|かんごし}をしています。
examples.english: My father is an office worker, and my mother is a nurse.

notes:
Colloquial spoken word for one's own home or family. Almost always written in hiragana when used in this sense. うちの + noun is the common pattern for referring to a family member or something belonging to one's household.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- うちに{帰|かえ}る: to go home
- うちで{食|た}べる: to eat at home
- うちの{子|こ}: my child / our kid
- うちの{会社|かいしゃ}: my company / our company
- うちの{犬|いぬ}: our dog

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {家|いえ}: house — refers to the building itself; more neutral
- {自宅|じたく}: one's own home — formal/written register
- {内|うち}: inside, within — different word entirely; separate entry
